tagline: Where Charleston Boulevard runs out of city and into sandstone.
intro: At the edge of Summerlin South, Route 159 stops being Charleston Boulevard, a city arterial, and goes on as a two-lane road curving around the foot of Red Rock Canyon. The red and cream sandstone peaks and walls stand up to 3,000 feet high, formed by thrust faults, the Keystone Thrust among them, and the Wilson Cliffs show to the west.

Then the road runs down the Cottonwood Valley, a side trail of the Old Spanish Trail, to the old company town of Blue Diamond. Roy Rogers and Trigger worked these rocks in Bells of San Angelo in 1947.

moments.title: Red Rock Canyon Scenic Loop
moments.text: From the visitor center a one-way loop runs 13 miles among the formations, past huge sandstone blocks left behind by an early quarry that never paid its way.

moments.title: Spring Mountain Ranch State Park
moments.text: Pack trains on the Spanish Trail camped by this spring-fed creek from the 1830s, and the park now keeps the ranch house, the blacksmith's shop and a chinchilla shed.

moments.title: Blue Diamond
moments.text: A gypsum company town begun in 1942, where the general store built that year for the miners keeps its original face and hangs the town's old photographs inside.
